title: Check yourself: what the compiler says about catch blocks

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when `catch (Exception e)` is written above `catch (IllegalArgumentException e)` on one try?

options.text: It compiles, and the JVM picks the closest match when one is thrown
options.says: The page says blocks are evaluated top to bottom, and this order is not accepted at all.

options.text: It compiles, and the lower block runs only after the upper one does
options.says: The page says the lower block could never be reached, and the order is not accepted.

options.text: It is refused by the compiler, since the lower block is unreachable
options.says: The page quotes the compiler: "exception IllegalArgumentException has already been caught".

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, what does `catch (NumberFormatException | IllegalArgumentException e)` do?

options.text: It compiles, and the first listed type is matched before the other
options.says: The page says this multi-catch does not compile at all.

options.text: It fails to compile, because one alternative subclasses the other
options.says: The page quotes: "Alternatives in a multi-catch statement cannot be related by subclassing".

options.text: It compiles, and the second listed type can never be matched
options.says: The page says alternatives related by subclassing are rejected by the compiler.
